name: Nwobodo Chukwuemeka Victor
feedback: D1: You catalogued only four of the ten findings (SQL injection A03/CWE-89, JWT alg:none A07/CWE-347, XXE A05/CWE-611, open redirect A01/CWE-601), and each class and CWE you gave is correct, which is good work. The cost is everything you left out: the unsalted MD5 hashing (A02/CWE-916 around line 66), the hardcoded JWT secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (CWE-798), no token expiry (CWE-613), the stored XSS with the cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443 (CWE-79), the path traversal to /etc/passwd (CWE-22), and the missing Secure/SameSite cookie flags (CWE-614) are all absent, and each missing finding costs its share. Your SQLi line reference (14 to 18) does not match the actual concatenated query around lines 64 to 67, and you never quote the offending source line, so that finding lands at half. The one thing you nailed is the decoy: you correctly named hash_equals() and proved it is constant-time and therefore sound, which is exactly the safe construct, so you earned full decoy credit there. D2: The chain is collapsed to four hops and is not reconciled to a single capture timestamp, so the grader cannot see recon at 02:14:08, the SQLi at 02:15:31, the bulk PII pull at 02:16:04, the stored XSS at 02:18:47, the open redirect at 02:21:13, or the file read at 02:24:02; reconstructing the chain against those exact lines is most of this deliverable. Your PoC payloads are generic rather than the verbatim strings from the capture, and you provided only two CVSS vectors. The SQLi vector string CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N is correct, but you labelled it 9.8 when that vector computes to about 9.1, since A:N means the bypass does not hit availability. Impact named 312 customers and the BoltCash six-week launch, but you gave no naira figure and no stated assumptions, so the financial picture (balances up to roughly 950k NGN summing to tens of millions) never appears. D3: The executive summary is readable and customer-focused, but it ends on regulatory risk rather than a customers-and-naira headline. The remediation ordering is your strongest section: you ordered by effort-to-risk and correctly put SQLi first because it breaks the chain at hop one despite JWT scoring higher, and you tied it to roughly two hours of work. Your two detection stopgaps name false-positive judgements but no exact log field. The serious problem is the disproved-decoy line: you wrote that login_verify_nonce() was the safe construct, and that function does not exist anywhere in the pack, which directly contradicts the correct hash_equals answer you gave in D1, so that row scores zero. D4: You answered the journalist, the written-record, and the colleague-evidence prompts in your own voice and anchored to the 312 affected customers, and you cited ISC2 Canon I by number in a load-bearing way, which is what was asked. You weakened it by naming the NDPA 2023 and the NDPC without the section numbers, so the 72-hour NDPC notification duty under section 40 and the data-subject notification under section 41 are missing, and the fourth prompt (the one action you would take regardless of your manager) is only lightly touched. The single most important fix: finish the catalogue. Find and quote all ten findings with their exact source lines and capture timestamps, because a four-finding catalogue cannot carry D1 or feed a complete D2 chain no matter how clean the four entries are.
